name: Samuel
bio:
Samuel was the son Elkanah and Hannah received through faithful prayer, dedicated to the LORD from infancy, who became the pivotal figure bridging the era of the judges and the beginning of Israel's monarchy — at once judge, priest, and one of the most influential prophets of the Old Testament.

## 👤 Identity and Background: A Child Given in Answer to Prayer, Dedicated from Infancy

His mother Hannah, childless and in anguish, prayed earnestly at the Shiloh sanctuary, vowing that if the LORD gave her a son, she would dedicate him to the LORD for life. The LORD answered her prayer, and she bore Samuel, whose name means "because I asked the LORD for him" (1 Samuel 1:10-20). Once weaned, Hannah, keeping her vow, brought Samuel to Shiloh and gave him to the priest Eli to serve the LORD for life (1 Samuel 1:24-28).

## 📖 Core Story: Called as a Prophet

1. **Called Three Times in the Night**: While still a boy serving under Eli, Samuel heard the LORD call his name three times in the night; at first he did not realize it was the LORD calling, until Eli taught him how to respond, and Samuel finally answered, "Speak, for your servant is listening" (1 Samuel 3:1-10).
2. **Receiving the Prophecy of Judgment on Eli's House**: The LORD told Samuel that he would carry out the judgment against Eli's house previously announced through a man of God; though afraid, Samuel told Eli everything exactly as he had heard it, and Eli responded in submission, "He is the LORD; let him do what is good in his eyes" (1 Samuel 3:11-18).
3. **Established as the LORD's Prophet**: As Samuel grew, the LORD was with him and let none of his words fail; all Israel from Dan to Beersheba recognized that Samuel was established as a prophet of the LORD (1 Samuel 3:19-20).

After the Philistines captured the ark and later returned it, Samuel gathered all Israel at Mizpah, urging the people to put away their foreign gods and turn to the LORD alone; as he offered sacrifice and prayed for them, the Philistines attacked, but the LORD thundered against them and threw them into confusion, and Israel pursued and defeated them. Samuel then set up a stone there, calling it Ebenezer, meaning "the LORD has helped us thus far" (1 Samuel 7:3-13). Samuel went on to judge Israel for the rest of his life, traveling each year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and building an altar to the LORD in his hometown of Ramah (1 Samuel 7:15-17).

Samuel went on to anoint both Saul and David as king, standing at the center of Israel's pivotal transition from direct rule by God to the institution of kingship — a story told in detail in 1 Samuel 8-16. When Samuel died in old age, all Israel gathered to mourn him and buried him at his home in Ramah (1 Samuel 25:1); his death also left David without this mentor and spiritual advisor, just as Saul's persecution of him was reaching its height.

## ✨ Key Character and Theological Significance

- **A Model of Obedient Listening to God's Word**: The defining trait of Samuel's entire life began with that boyhood response — "Speak, for your servant is listening" — a posture of prayer that believers, in both the New Testament and throughout history, have continually sought to imitate in seeking to know God's heart.

Samuel's emergence marked Israel's gradual transition from the chaotic, disordered era of the judges into a new stage led by prophets and governed by kings, and his life would continue to shape Israel's history for generations to come.

Even after his death, Samuel left one final, startling mark on Israel's history: as the Philistines massed for war, Saul sought guidance from the LORD and received no answer, so — in violation of the very law he himself had once enforced banning mediums — he disguised himself and visited a medium at Endor by night, asking her to summon Samuel's spirit. Samuel's spirit told Saul that the LORD had torn the kingdom from him because of his disobedience and given it to David, and declared that Saul and his sons would join him in death the next day (1 Samuel 28:3-19). Though Samuel had already died, the words he had spoken in life were fulfilled at the very end of Saul's, bringing a haunting coda to the life of Israel's first great prophet.
